lines.trans: Wait a minute... What are you doing here at all?
Hello, I am simply strolling through your restaurant.
How did you dare to come into my establishment?
I was just chatting for a long time with your head chef.
And what did you talk with him about?
He is persistently inviting me to work with him.
You are joking, the chef never takes novices!
Here I stand and think, whether to agree or not.
Do you dare to still doubt our level?
Frankly speaking, your kitchen seems a bit basic to me.
Our restaurant is one of the best in Moscow!
Then I, perhaps, will agree to show my talent.
I will personally check these ridiculous words right now!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to chatter, chat, talk idly', paired with 'поболтать'.

examples.text: Не словом, а делом! Все болтают, а я работаю.
examples.trans: Not in word, but in deed! Everyone chatters, while I work.

meanings.note: habitually or in general
'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where)
+ accusative (where to)

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: polite (вы) or plural

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: for emphasis

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: pointing at something
emphasis

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you

гулять.gloss: to walk, to go for a walk

meanings.en: to walk, to stroll, to be outside
meanings.note: гулять с собакой = to walk the dog

examples.trans: A girl walks a little dog there.
Let's go for a walk in the park.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: He talks for a long time.
We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
ещё больше = even more

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ведение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'establishment, institution' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это небольшой комплимент от нашего заведения.
examples.trans: This is a small gift from our establishment.

examples.text: Это очень популярное заведение в городе.
examples.trans: This is a very popular establishment in town.

examples.text: Как ты посмел прийти в моё заведение?
examples.trans: How did you dare to come into my establishment?

meanings.note: звать на помощь = to call for help
как тебя зовут? = what's your name? меня зовут ... = my name is ...
location
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.
+ dative

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me
кажется as a parenthetical word

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: question word
как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: the room
русская кухня = Russian cuisine

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: Anikeev came here in person, and what?

examples.text: Пятнадцать лет мы просим новое здание! Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: For fifteen years we've been asking for a new building! Anikeev came here in person, and what?

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: agrees with the thing owned
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стойчиво'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Он настойчиво зовёт меня работать к себе.
examples.trans: He is persistently inviting me to work with him.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'лепый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('absurd, ridiculous').

examples.text: Я сейчас лично проверю эти нелепые слова!
examples.trans: I will personally check these ridiculous words right now!

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive
used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

meanings.note: новичкам везёт = beginners get lucky

examples.text: Говорят, что всем новичкам всегда везёт.
examples.trans: They say that all beginners always get lucky.

examples.text: Ты шутишь, шеф никогда не берёт новичков!
examples.trans: You are joking, the chef never takes novices!

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
for masculine and neuter things

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: case forms
in 'по поводу' + genitive
+ dative
'по телефону'

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: подожди! = wait!

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: я, пожалуй, пойду = I think I'll be going

examples.trans: All right, I think I'll be going.

examples.text: Ладно, я, пожалуй, пойду. Пока, Нина!
examples.trans: All right, I think I'll go. Bye, Nina!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.note: + infinitive; как ты посмел? = how dare you?

examples.text: Да как ты посмел? Это собака маленькой девочки!
examples.trans: How dare you! That's a little girl's dog!

meanings.note: informal: family and friends

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: on foot, once

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to check, to test', paired with 'проверять'.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву. Паяльник проверь.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood. Check the soldering iron.

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy
это просто = it's easy

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стоватый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('simple, basic, rustic').

examples.trans: The kitchen seems a bit basic.

examples.text: Честно говоря, ваша кухня мне кажется простоватой.
examples.trans: Frankly speaking, your kitchen seems a bit basic to me.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.en: to talk, to speak, to have a conversation
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'говаривать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to talk, to speak'.

examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

examples.text: А что вы так грубо разговариваете?
examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

meanings.note: dining establishment

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: reflexive; no nominative

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: 'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word
'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'меть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to dare', paired with 'посметь'.

examples.text: Ты смеешь ещё сомневаться в нашем уровне?
examples.trans: Do you dare to still doubt our level?

examples.text: Никто не смеет оскорблять мою высокую кухню!
examples.trans: Nobody dares insult my haute cuisine!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to agree', paired with 'соглашаться'.

examples.trans: Admit it / Don't you agree, that's much better.

examples.text: Это гораздо лучше, чем двенадцать лет. Согласитесь?
examples.trans: That's much better than twelve years. Don't you agree?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оглашаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to agree', paired with 'согласиться'.

examples.text: Вот стою и думаю, соглашаться или нет.
examples.trans: Here I stand and think, whether to agree or not.

meanings.note: сомневаться в + prepositional
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

meanings.note: у него есть талант

examples.text: У этой девочки большой талант к музыке.
examples.trans: This girl has a great talent for music.

examples.text: Потому что твой папа прав! У тебя нет таланта.
examples.trans: Because your dad is right! You have no talent.

meanings.note: to someone you call ты

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: at that time

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
one person, informal

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: case forms

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ровень'). Common masculine noun meaning 'level' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you want me to tell you honestly?

examples.text: Всё честно, Лёха. Взрослые не умеют ждать.
examples.trans: It's all fair, Lyokha. Grown-ups can't wait.

meanings.note: question word
conjunction

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: informal

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: chief cook in a professional kitchen

examples.trans: Our head chef is cooking lunch.
The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

examples.text: Они привели нового шеф-повара прямо из Индии.
examples.trans: They brought a new chef straight from India.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to joke', paired with 'пошутить'.

examples.text: Шутишь? Правда, скажи, где деньги? Меня наняли.
examples.trans: Are you joking? Seriously, tell me, where's the money? They hired me.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
